notes: The 3V3 rail on bb2 is one strip, so the three red wires go to three different holes of it (tp.1, tp.2, tp.3).

E8 is kept on purpose; it is not a real problem. The reader's 3V3 pin is a 3.3 V OUTPUT in this circuit. It only feeds the two 4.7k I2C pull-ups, exactly as the circuit image shows (reader '3V' pin to the pull-up resistors). Nothing supplies the board through 3V3. The reader is powered at 5 V over its own USB cable, which is inside its 4.5-21 V supply range. Pull-ups to 3V3 are right for a 3.3 V logic board, and the image is the authority on this wire.
I2C on the Nano 33 IoT: SDA = A4, SCL = A5. SCL of reader and writer meet on bb1 strip 10t; SDA of both meet on bb1 strip 12t. GND of the two boards is wired directly together, as in the image.

The manual lists 2 mini breadboards and 10 jumper wires but the image shows neither breadboards nor the exact wire layout. I assumed bb1 carries the I2C bus and bb2 carries the pull-ups and 3V3 rail; the extra 4 jumper wires are the bus-to-pull-up links and pull-up-to-rail links. Exact hole positions are my choice.
The boards are not shown seated in a breadboard, so wires go from the board header pins to breadboard holes.
Each board is powered and programmed over its own USB cable from the computer. The computer is not a graph part, so the USB cables only connect to the boards' USB ports.
